question: Burn percentage in an adult is best estimated using:
subject: Medical-Surgical

explanations.A: Wallace's Rule of Nines divides adult body surface area into multiples of 9 (head 9%, each arm 9%, each leg 18%, anterior trunk 18%, posterior trunk 18%, perineum 1%) for rapid bedside burn estimation.
explanations.B: More accurate but used for children and detailed assessment, not the bedside default in adults.
explanations.C: Patient's palm ≈ 1% TBSA — useful for small/scattered burns only.
explanations.D: Calculates fluid volume after % TBSA is determined, not the % itself.

citation: ATLS 10e; Brunner & Suddarth 14e — Emergency and Trauma Nursing
explanation: Wallace's Rule of Nines divides adult body surface area into multiples of 9 (head 9%, each arm 9%, each leg 18%, anterior trunk 18%, posterior trunk 18%, perineum 1%) for rapid bedside burn estimation.

question: Cardiac troponin level is most useful in diagnosing:
subject: Medical-Surgical

explanations.A: Troponin I and T are highly specific cardiac muscle proteins released after myocyte injury; they rise within 3-6 h, peak at 24 h, and remain elevated up to 10-14 days, making them the gold-standard MI marker.
explanations.B: D-dimer and CT pulmonary angiogram are the diagnostic tools.
explanations.C: BNP/NT-proBNP is the failure-specific marker.
explanations.D: Diagnosed by ECG (diffuse ST elevation) and echo, not troponin.

citation: Brunner & Suddarth 14e — Textbook of Medical-Surgical Nursing
explanation: Troponin I and T are highly specific cardiac muscle proteins released after myocyte injury; they rise within 3-6 h, peak at 24 h, and remain elevated up to 10-14 days, making them the gold-standard MI marker.

question: Which type of shock results from a severe allergic reaction?
subject: Medical-Surgical

explanations.A: Pump failure (e.g., post-MI), not allergy.
explanations.B: Anaphylactic (distributive) shock is an IgE-mediated hypersensitivity causing massive vasodilation, capillary leak and bronchospasm; first-line treatment is IM adrenaline 0.5 mg in the anterolateral thigh.
explanations.C: Caused by blood/fluid loss.
explanations.D: Caused by overwhelming infection and dysregulated host response.

citation: ATLS 10e; Brunner & Suddarth 14e — Emergency and Trauma Nursing
explanation: Anaphylactic (distributive) shock is an IgE-mediated hypersensitivity causing massive vasodilation, capillary leak and bronchospasm; first-line treatment is IM adrenaline 0.5 mg in the anterolateral thigh.

question: Mannitol is given to a head-injury patient mainly to:
subject: Medical-Surgical

explanations.A: Not its primary indication.
explanations.B: Not a chronotropic drug.
explanations.C: Mannitol is an osmotic diuretic that draws fluid from brain tissue into the intravascular space, lowering ICP. Typical dose 0.25-1 g/kg IV over 15-30 min; monitor serum osmolality and urine output.
explanations.D: Antipyretics or cooling, not mannitol.

citation: Brunner & Suddarth 14e — Textbook of Medical-Surgical Nursing
explanation: Mannitol is an osmotic diuretic that draws fluid from brain tissue into the intravascular space, lowering ICP. Typical dose 0.25-1 g/kg IV over 15-30 min; monitor serum osmolality and urine output.

question: The most common form of dementia is:
subject: Psychiatric

explanations.A: Alzheimer's accounts for 60-70% of dementia worldwide; it is characterised by amyloid plaques, neurofibrillary tangles and progressive loss of recent memory and executive function.
explanations.B: Second most common (≈20%); stepwise decline after strokes.
explanations.C: Younger onset, prominent personality/behaviour changes — less common.
explanations.D: Visual hallucinations and parkinsonism — less common.

citation: Ahuja's A Short Textbook of Psychiatry 8e
explanation: Alzheimer's accounts for 60-70% of dementia worldwide; it is characterised by amyloid plaques, neurofibrillary tangles and progressive loss of recent memory and executive function.

question: First aid for a chemical splash to the eye is to:
options: Wash the eye thoroughly with water
Cover the eye with a sterile pad
subject: Medical-Surgical

explanations.A: Immediate copious irrigation with clean water or saline for at least 15-20 minutes dilutes the chemical, neutralises pH and is the single most important measure to limit corneal damage.
explanations.B: Done after irrigation and ophthalmology review.
explanations.C: Trapping chemical against the eye worsens injury.
explanations.D: Delaying irrigation allows continuing chemical burn.

citation: Potter & Perry Fundamentals of Nursing 10e; Kozier & Erb Fundamentals of Nursing 11e
explanation: Immediate copious irrigation with clean water or saline for at least 15-20 minutes dilutes the chemical, neutralises pH and is the single most important measure to limit corneal damage.

question: Universal blood donor group is:
subject: Medical-Surgical

explanations.A: Lacks A/B antigens but Rh+ can sensitise Rh-negative recipients.
explanations.B: O-negative red cells carry neither A, B nor Rh(D) antigens, so they can be transfused to recipients of any ABO/Rh group in emergencies — hence 'universal donor'.
explanations.C: AB+ is the universal recipient, not donor.
explanations.D: AB negative is universal plasma donor, not RBC donor.

citation: Brunner & Suddarth 14e — Textbook of Medical-Surgical Nursing
explanation: O-negative red cells carry neither A, B nor Rh(D) antigens, so they can be transfused to recipients of any ABO/Rh group in emergencies — hence 'universal donor'.

question: A pressure ulcer with exposed bone, tendon, or muscle is classified as:
subject: Fundamentals

explanations.A: Non-blanchable erythema, intact skin.
explanations.B: Partial-thickness loss of dermis (shallow open ulcer).
explanations.C: Full-thickness skin loss with visible subcutaneous fat — bone/tendon NOT exposed.
explanations.D: NPIAP Stage IV is full-thickness loss with exposed bone, tendon or muscle, often with undermining/tunneling and high risk of osteomyelitis.

citation: Gray’s Anatomy for Students 4e; Guyton & Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology 14e
explanation: NPIAP Stage IV is full-thickness loss with exposed bone, tendon or muscle, often with undermining/tunneling and high risk of osteomyelitis.

question: Which procedure mandatorily requires surgical asepsis?
subject: Fundamentals

explanations.A: Clean (medical asepsis) only.
explanations.B: The bladder is normally sterile; introducing a Foley breaches that barrier and demands sterile gloves, sterile drape, sterile catheter and sterile lubricant to prevent CAUTI.
explanations.C: Clean technique sufficient.
explanations.D: Clean technique sufficient; gut is non-sterile.

citation: Potter & Perry Fundamentals of Nursing 10e
explanation: The bladder is normally sterile; introducing a Foley breaches that barrier and demands sterile gloves, sterile drape, sterile catheter and sterile lubricant to prevent CAUTI.

question: Anterior fontanelle in an infant normally closes by:
subject: Pediatric

explanations.A: Posterior fontanelle closes by 2-3 months — not anterior.
explanations.B: The diamond-shaped anterior fontanelle (≈3-4 cm at birth) closes between 12 and 18 months; delayed closure suggests rickets, hypothyroidism or hydrocephalus.
explanations.C: Beyond normal range — raises suspicion of pathology.
explanations.D: Far beyond normal range.

citation: Ghai Essential Pediatrics 9e — Growth, Development and Neonatology
explanation: The diamond-shaped anterior fontanelle (≈3-4 cm at birth) closes between 12 and 18 months; delayed closure suggests rickets, hypothyroidism or hydrocephalus.

question: Failure of the foramen ovale to close at birth results in:
subject: Pediatric

explanations.A: Defect is in the interventricular septum, embryologically distinct.
explanations.B: Persistence of the ductus arteriosus (between aorta and pulmonary artery), not foramen ovale.
explanations.C: The foramen ovale is the fetal opening between the two atria; failure to close after birth produces a secundum-type ASD with left-to-right shunt.
explanations.D: TOF is a four-component anomaly involving VSD, PS, RVH and overriding aorta — not foramen ovale.

citation: Ghai Essential Pediatrics 9e — Growth, Development and Neonatology
explanation: The foramen ovale is the fetal opening between the two atria; failure to close after birth produces a secundum-type ASD with left-to-right shunt.

question: Touching the cheek of a newborn elicits which reflex?
subject: Pediatric

explanations.A: Triggered by sudden loss of support or loud noise (startle response).
explanations.B: Stroking the cheek/corner of mouth makes the baby turn head toward the stimulus and open mouth — a feeding reflex present until ~3-4 months.
explanations.C: Elicited by stroking the sole of the foot.
explanations.D: Elicited by turning the head while supine ('fencer' posture).

citation: Ghai Essential Pediatrics 9e — Growth, Development and Neonatology
explanation: Stroking the cheek/corner of mouth makes the baby turn head toward the stimulus and open mouth — a feeding reflex present until ~3-4 months.

question: Pyloric stenosis in an infant typically presents with:
subject: Pediatric

explanations.A: Implies obstruction below the ampulla of Vater — not pyloric.
explanations.B: Suggests intussusception or colitis.
explanations.C: Hypertrophic pyloric stenosis (typically 2-8 weeks old) obstructs gastric outflow above the ampulla, producing forceful non-bilious projectile vomiting, hypochloraemic metabolic alkalosis and a palpable 'olive' in the epigastrium.
explanations.D: Not the hallmark; vomiting dominates the picture.

citation: Ghai Essential Pediatrics 9e — Growth, Development and Neonatology
explanation: Hypertrophic pyloric stenosis (typically 2-8 weeks old) obstructs gastric outflow above the ampulla, producing forceful non-bilious projectile vomiting, hypochloraemic metabolic alkalosis and a palpable 'olive' in the epigastrium.

question: Severe dehydration in a child is best managed by:
subject: Pediatric

explanations.A: Used in some/no dehydration (Plan A/B).
explanations.B: Lacks electrolytes; can worsen hyponatraemia.
explanations.C: WHO Plan C for severe dehydration: IV Ringer Lactate 100 mL/kg — first 30 mL/kg in 30 min (or 1 h if <12 months) and remaining 70 mL/kg over the next 2.5-5 h, with frequent reassessment.
explanations.D: Inadequate replacement when shock-grade fluid loss has occurred.

citation: Ghai Essential Pediatrics 9e — Growth, Development and Neonatology
explanation: WHO Plan C for severe dehydration: IV Ringer Lactate 100 mL/kg — first 30 mL/kg in 30 min (or 1 h if <12 months) and remaining 70 mL/kg over the next 2.5-5 h, with frequent reassessment.

question: The hormone responsible for ovulation surge in mid-cycle is:
subject: OBG

explanations.A: FSH stimulates follicular growth in the early follicular phase.
explanations.B: A sharp LH surge ~24-36 h before ovulation triggers rupture of the dominant follicle and release of the secondary oocyte.
explanations.C: Rising estrogen triggers the LH surge but does not itself rupture the follicle.
explanations.D: Dominant in the luteal phase, after ovulation.

citation: DC Dutta's Textbook of Gynecology 8e
explanation: A sharp LH surge ~24-36 h before ovulation triggers rupture of the dominant follicle and release of the secondary oocyte.

question: Bluish discoloration of the cervix and vagina in early pregnancy is called:
subject: OBG

explanations.A: Softening of the lower uterine segment (~6-12 weeks).
explanations.B: Softening of the cervix.
explanations.C: Chadwick's sign — violet/bluish discolouration of the vagina, vulva and cervix from increased pelvic vascularity, visible at ~6-8 weeks.
explanations.D: Pulsation in lateral fornices due to uterine artery.

citation: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e / Gynecology 8e
explanation: Chadwick's sign — violet/bluish discolouration of the vagina, vulva and cervix from increased pelvic vascularity, visible at ~6-8 weeks.

question: If LMP is 20 June, the expected date of delivery by Naegele's rule is:
subject: OBG

explanations.A: Wrong subtraction of months — too early.
explanations.B: Naegele's rule: LMP + 9 months + 7 days. 20 June + 7 days = 27 June, plus 9 months = 27 March.
explanations.C: Forgot to add 7 days.
explanations.D: Added two extra weeks instead of seven days.

citation: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e — Obstetric Management
explanation: Naegele's rule: LMP + 9 months + 7 days. 20 June + 7 days = 27 June, plus 9 months = 27 March.

question: First stage of labour ends with:
subject: OBG

explanations.A: Marks the start of the first stage, not its end.
explanations.B: Can occur at any point and is not the defining endpoint.
explanations.C: First stage runs from regular contractions to full (10 cm) cervical dilatation; the second stage then runs to delivery of the baby.
explanations.D: That is the end of the third stage.

citation: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e — Obstetric Management
explanation: First stage runs from regular contractions to full (10 cm) cervical dilatation; the second stage then runs to delivery of the baby.

question: Earliest sign of placental separation in the third stage of labour is:
options: Sudden gush of blood per vagina
subject: OBG

explanations.A: A sudden small gush of blood from the vagina (along with cord lengthening and fundal change) is the classic earliest sign that the placenta has detached from the uterine wall.
explanations.B: Non-specific; not a separation sign.
explanations.C: Fundus rises and becomes globular when placenta separates — it does not fall.
explanations.D: Pain is variable and not diagnostic.

citation: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e — Obstetric Management
explanation: A sudden small gush of blood from the vagina (along with cord lengthening and fundal change) is the classic earliest sign that the placenta has detached from the uterine wall.

question: Abnormal accumulation of fluid in the pleural cavity is called:
subject: Medical-Surgical

explanations.A: Air in the pleural space, not fluid.
explanations.B: Pleural effusion is any abnormal collection of fluid (transudate or exudate) in the pleural cavity — the umbrella term being asked.
explanations.C: Specifically blood in the pleural space.
explanations.D: Specifically pus in the pleural space.

citation: Brunner & Suddarth 14e — Textbook of Medical-Surgical Nursing
explanation: Pleural effusion is any abnormal collection of fluid (transudate or exudate) in the pleural cavity — the umbrella term being asked.

question: VDRL test is used to diagnose:
subject: Microbiology

explanations.A: Diagnosed by Gram stain and culture/NAAT for Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
explanations.B: ELISA/Western blot detects HIV antibodies.
explanations.C: VDRL (Venereal Disease Research Laboratory) is a non-treponemal flocculation test that detects reagin antibodies against cardiolipin, used to screen for syphilis (Treponema pallidum).
explanations.D: Schick test is for diphtheria immunity, not VDRL.

citation: Ananthanarayan & Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology 11e
explanation: VDRL (Venereal Disease Research Laboratory) is a non-treponemal flocculation test that detects reagin antibodies against cardiolipin, used to screen for syphilis (Treponema pallidum).

question: Schick test is used to diagnose susceptibility to:
subject: Microbiology

explanations.A: Mantoux/PPD detects TB exposure.
explanations.B: No analogous skin test — antibody titres used.
explanations.C: Diagnosed clinically and by PCR/culture.
explanations.D: Schick test injects diphtheria toxin intradermally; lack of erythema/induration after 48-72 h indicates immunity — historically used to assess diphtheria susceptibility.

citation: Ananthanarayan & Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology 11e
explanation: Schick test injects diphtheria toxin intradermally; lack of erythema/induration after 48-72 h indicates immunity — historically used to assess diphtheria susceptibility.

question: Rice-water stools are characteristic of:
subject: Community Health

explanations.A: Causes blood- and mucus-streaked stools, not rice-water.
explanations.B: Vibrio cholerae enterotoxin produces voluminous painless watery diarrhoea — colourless, odourless, with mucous flecks resembling water in which rice has been washed.
explanations.C: Pea-soup stools or constipation, with stepwise fever.
explanations.D: Shigella causes small-volume bloody mucoid stools with tenesmus.

citation: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine 26e
explanation: Vibrio cholerae enterotoxin produces voluminous painless watery diarrhoea — colourless, odourless, with mucous flecks resembling water in which rice has been washed.

question: Hepatitis A is transmitted mainly through the:
subject: Community Health

explanations.A: Hepatitis A virus is shed in stool and ingested via contaminated food/water; outbreaks are linked to poor sanitation and shellfish.
explanations.B: Major route for HBV/HCV/HIV, not HAV.
explanations.C: Major route for HBV/HCV.
explanations.D: Important for HBV — not Hepatitis A.

citation: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine 26e
explanation: Hepatitis A virus is shed in stool and ingested via contaminated food/water; outbreaks are linked to poor sanitation and shellfish.

question: DOTS strategy under RNTCP/NTEP for tuberculosis represents which level of prevention?
subject: Community Health

explanations.A: Targets risk-factor emergence in unaffected populations.
explanations.B: Vaccination (BCG) and health education would be primary.
explanations.C: DOTS detects active TB cases early and treats them with directly observed short-course chemotherapy, which halts disease progression and breaks transmission — the definition of secondary prevention.
explanations.D: Pulmonary rehabilitation in post-TB lung disease would be tertiary.

citation: MoHFW National TB Elimination Programme — Technical and Operational Guidelines
explanation: DOTS detects active TB cases early and treats them with directly observed short-course chemotherapy, which halts disease progression and breaks transmission — the definition of secondary prevention.

question: One 0.5 g chlorine tablet effectively disinfects how much water?
subject: Community Health

explanations.A: Underestimates chlorine potency.
explanations.B: Standard dose is higher than this.
explanations.C: Common distractor — not WHO/IPHS specification.
explanations.D: WHO/IPHS guidance: a 0.5 g (500 mg) chlorine tablet at standard demand provides residual chlorine adequate for ~20 L of water after 30 min contact time.

citation: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine 26e
explanation: WHO/IPHS guidance: a 0.5 g (500 mg) chlorine tablet at standard demand provides residual chlorine adequate for ~20 L of water after 30 min contact time.

question: Receiving readymade antibodies from another source represents:
subject: Microbiology

explanations.A: Antibodies produced after natural infection.
explanations.B: Maternal IgG across placenta or via breast milk.
explanations.C: Antibodies produced by host after vaccination.
explanations.D: Administered preformed antibodies (e.g., anti-tetanus serum, anti-rabies immunoglobulin, monoclonal antibodies) give rapid but short-lived protection — artificial passive immunity.

explanation: Administered preformed antibodies (e.g., anti-tetanus serum, anti-rabies immunoglobulin, monoclonal antibodies) give rapid but short-lived protection — artificial passive immunity.

question: Lithium is the drug of choice for which psychiatric condition?
subject: Psychiatric

explanations.A: Antipsychotics (e.g., risperidone) are first line.
explanations.B: Lithium remains the gold-standard mood stabiliser for acute mania and long-term prophylaxis in bipolar disorder; therapeutic range 0.6-1.2 mEq/L — monitor for nephrotoxicity, thyroid dysfunction, tremor.
explanations.C: SSRIs/SNRIs are first-line antidepressants.
explanations.D: SSRIs and CBT — not lithium.

explanation: Lithium remains the gold-standard mood stabiliser for acute mania and long-term prophylaxis in bipolar disorder; therapeutic range 0.6-1.2 mEq/L — monitor for nephrotoxicity, thyroid dysfunction, tremor.

question: Hierarchy of needs theory was proposed by:
subject: Fundamentals

explanations.A: Proposed psychoanalytic theory and the id-ego-superego model.
explanations.B: Maslow (1943) arranged human needs into a five-level pyramid — physiological, safety, love/belonging, esteem, self-actualisation — widely used in nursing to prioritise care.
explanations.C: Proposed eight psychosocial stages of development.
explanations.D: Proposed classical conditioning.

citation: Potter & Perry Fundamentals of Nursing 10e
explanation: Maslow (1943) arranged human needs into a five-level pyramid — physiological, safety, love/belonging, esteem, self-actualisation — widely used in nursing to prioritise care.

question: Best position for a rectal examination is:
subject: Fundamentals

explanations.A: Does not expose the anal canal adequately.
explanations.B: Used for respiratory comfort — unsuitable for rectal access.
explanations.C: Knee-chest (genupectoral) position elevates the buttocks and uses gravity to displace abdominal viscera, giving the best exposure of the anus and rectum for proctoscopy/sigmoidoscopy. Left lateral (Sims) is the next best alternative.
explanations.D: Provides poor visualisation and patient access compared with knee-chest.

citation: Potter & Perry Fundamentals of Nursing 10e; Kozier & Erb Fundamentals of Nursing 11e
explanation: Knee-chest (genupectoral) position elevates the buttocks and uses gravity to displace abdominal viscera, giving the best exposure of the anus and rectum for proctoscopy/sigmoidoscopy. Left lateral (Sims) is the next best alternative.
